children: , the enterprise software company, pushed its AI strategy into a finance task where mistakes matter: accounting for complex trades. It is working with Japanese trading company ITOCHU on the first use cases. SAP's U.S. shares rose about 1% to $211.10 at 11.20am ET time on Friday.

The work starts with raw-material transactions. SAP's system pulls together documents and business context, then suggests the general-ledger account and commission details for a finance specialist to review. That human check is central: an answer that looks plausible still has to hold up through the close and an audit. SAP's wider push into finance agents gives this project a bigger stage, but ITOCHU is a test of whether the tools can handle a real trading workflow.

The valuation picture shows SAP at $211.10, 17.77% below its $256.72 GF Value estimate. That gap may catch an investor's eye; this project alone cannot close it. SAP has yet to disclose the deployment's price, transaction volume or financial contribution. The payoff to watch is whether a process built for ITOCHU becomes a product SAP can sell repeatedly.

title: SAP Stock Rises as ITOCHU Tests Finance Agents
